$comment: The §17 demo set-piece from Docs/Project_Vaidhya_Technical_Architecture_v1.md. This is the definition of done for the whole project. Lanes claim steps via demo_steps_done in agents/status/*.md frontmatter. Do not renumber steps — the numbers are referenced from status files.

steps.title: Unplug Node A's wifi, on camera
steps.detail: Everything from here to step 6 happens with no internet. This is one of the three steps that actually wins it.

steps.title: Patient logs in, nurse enters vitals: SpO2 91, temp 38.9
steps.detail: Phone + OTP 123456. Two urgency flags now armed.

steps.title: Voicebot greets and converses in Malayalam
steps.detail: Transcript panel shows Malayalam AND its English clinical translation side by side.

steps.title: Rules engine visibly branches on SpO2 91
steps.detail: Bot goes straight to respiratory questions; on-screen badge reads 'fired rule: SpO2 < 92'. The point is that it is not a black box.

steps.title: Nurse-finding request times out gracefully
steps.detail: Bot asks for a finding, nurse does not respond, after 20s it re-prompts, then proceeds with not_obtained. Say out loud: the session never stalls on a missing test.

steps.title: Report generates — Urgent (2 flags) — with no internet
steps.detail: One of the three steps that actually wins it.

steps.title: Plug wifi back in — outbox flushes, patient appears in the doctor's queue tagged Urgent
steps.detail: Offline sync on reconnect. The single hardest claim to fake, and the third step that wins it.

steps.title: Doctor clicks Consult Specialist AI
steps.detail: Structured opinion returns with confidence and evidence trace.

steps.title: Doctor types a question over MQTT; voicebot speaks it in Malayalam
steps.detail: Patient answers, the English answer appears on the doctor's screen. Needs T1's relay on the edge side.

steps.title: Doctor issues a prescription; it appears immediately in the patient portal
steps.detail: Full medication list, viewable and printable. This is how the prescription is delivered — nothing about it depends on SMS.

steps.title: Nearby pharmacies with per-medicine stock; patient picks one; it lands in that pharmacy's queue
steps.detail: Then the pharmacist marks it fulfilled and bills it. The patient can now simply walk to that shop.

steps.title: Twilio medication reminder to a real phone, then the follow-up ~90s later
steps.detail: Reminders ABOUT the prescription, not the prescription itself. Highest external risk in the project — DLT/trial restrictions can block this for reasons unrelated to your code.

steps.title: Close on the analytics dashboard: the anomaly spike, highlighted
